USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Technique before escalation

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A patient reports persistent asthma symptoms despite being prescribed an ICS-containing inhaler. At review, he actuates the metered-dose device after finishing inhalation, so little medicine reaches the lungs. What should be addressed before assuming pharmacologic treatment failure?

  1. Immediately label all corticosteroids ineffective
  2. Replace the controller with chronic oral antibiotics
  3. Take every dose twice without changing technique
  4. Stop all controller treatment permanently
  5. Correct inhaler technique and assess adherence
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Correct inhaler technique and assess adherence

Poor delivery can explain apparent lack of efficacy and should be corrected before unnecessary escalation.

Understanding the options

Correct inhaler technique and assess adherence
Poor delivery can explain apparent lack of efficacy and should be corrected before unnecessary escalation.
Immediately label all corticosteroids ineffective
The medication may not be reaching its target.
Replace the controller with chronic oral antibiotics
Antibiotics do not correct inhaler technique or routine asthma inflammation.
Take every dose twice without changing technique
More poorly delivered doses do not resolve the cause.
Stop all controller treatment permanently
The problem calls for technique correction, not abandonment of control.
